[NTST.3.3] A mock-clock mutation sets the mock clock and is not itself a
sample ([LTIM.2.8.4]): it emits no event and records nothing. The next input
or pump samples the clock source, reads the value the mutation left, and
records it as a `ClockAdvance` carrying both clocks when it differs from the
previous sample ([LTIM.2.8.5], [RFCS.10.1]), with the `DS_EV_TICK` stream
event that sample drives. So a test writes the trace a live run through the
same clock values writes, and two mutations between samples leave one record.
